newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Kucan asks Drnovsek to form government.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Kucan asks Drnovsek to form government.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan said on Monday he had given a mandate to acting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek to form the next government after inconclusive general elections in November.
"I name Janez Drnovsek as candidate for prime minister... He is the leader of the party that won most votes in the election," Kucan told a news conference.
Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats emerged as the strongest party in the November 10 general election, winning 25 of 90 parliamentary seats.
But Drnovsek is faced with an alliance of three right-wing parties who together won 45 seats in the former Yugoslav republic's second general election since independence in 1991.
With one seat short of an absolute majority, the alliance headed by conservative People's Party leader Marjan Podobnik, will be reluctant to give up the fight to form the next administration.
Drnovsek, 46, needs to win over at least one of the rightwing parties to break the deadlock. Parliament has to vote to back Drnovsek as prime minister within seven days.
